sentences.text:
Respondent :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Petitioner :- Arun Kumar Tripathi,Shams Uz Zaman

Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.
Hon'ble Saurabh Srivastava,J.
1. Heard learned counsel for parties.

2. This petitioner has been preferred with the prayer to issue an order or direction in exercise of supervisory power vested in this Court under Article 227 of the Constitution of India, setting aside the order dated 24.05.2024 passed by C.J.M. Baghpat in case No. 2552 of 2021, under sections 498A, 323, 376, 307, 504, 506, IPC and 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Badout, District Baghpat.
3.
Learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that petitioner no. 1 is husband of respondent no. 2.

Respondent no. 2 lodged a FIR against the petitioners who are husband, father-in-law,

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
After investigation, charge sheet was submitted against the petitioners under sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 IPC and 3/4 D.P. Act whereupon learned court has taken cognizance on dated 23.02.2021.
4.

Petitioners challenged the said charge sheet by way of filing Application under Section 482 no.
29773 of 2021 before this Court which is pending to be adjudicated.

Meanwhile, respondent no. 2 filed an application under Section 323 Cr.P.C. before the court of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Baghpat for adding sections 376, 307 IPC in the said case crime and the same was allowed vide order dated 24.05.2024 which has been challenged through the instant petition.
5. Learned counsel for petitioner challenged the impugned orders on the ground that injured was medically examined by the medical officer and as per medical report, injuries are simple in nature.

Order dated 24.05.2024 has been passed without applying judicial mind and in arbitrary manner hence is liable to be set aside.
6.
Per contra, learned AGA vehemently opposed the prayer sought through the instant petition and supported the order impugned.

7. After hearing the rival submissions extended by learned counsels for the parties and perusing the records, this Court is of the opinion that order dated 24.05.2024 does not contain any infirmity and none of the grounds raised through the instant petition are convincing enough within the ambit of law so as to attract the interference of this Court.
Order impugned has been passed after due consideration of materials available on record.

8. Lastly, learned counsel for the petitioners prayed that the present petition may be decided finally with a direction to the court concerned that in case petitioners surrender before it and apply for bail,
their bail application may be considered and decided expeditiously in accordance with law,
including the law laid down in the case of Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another (2022 SCC OnLine SC 825) to which learned counsel for opposite parties have no objection.
9.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another (2022 SCC OnLine SC 825)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the aforesaid, the instant petition is dismissed with a direction to the court concerned that in case, the petitioners surrender before the court concerned within a period of 30 days from today and apply for bail, their bail application shall be considered and decided expeditiously in accordance with settled law.
10. However, it is made clear that till 30 days from today, no coercive action shall be taken against the petitioners herein.
